summary: Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied at the University of Iowa and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He served as dean and professor emeritus at UT Austin, provost at the University of Kansas, and president of the Field Museum.

Sinologist Richard Wilhelm studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen. He served as a visiting professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924, which he founded in 1925.

Richard von Garbe was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Marienstiftsgymnasium, the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Hermann Günther Grassmann, and the University of Königsberg. He held posts at Königsberg and succeeded Roth at Tübingen (1895–1927).

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.

Rikizan Ishikawa was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1973, where he later served as Professor of Buddhist Studies from around 1990 to 1997.

Ringu Tulku is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. His teachers included Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and he has taught at Naropa University.
Rinzin Thargyal is a Tibetologist who earned a Magister degree at the University of Oslo by 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004) under Lambert Schmithausen, later holding posts at the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at UW–Milwaukee and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. She held posts at UW–Madison and served as Professor Emerita at UW–Eau Claire (1979–1998).

Rizong Sras Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who trained monastically at Drepung Loseling Monastery under the 14th Dalai Lama, Losal Ling Khen Zur Jampal Sampel, and Pema Gyaltsen. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College and Drepung Loseling.

Rob Linrothe is a Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and art history scholar. He studied at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago (PhD 1992). He held posts at the National Palace Museum, Skidmore College, Rubin Museum, and Northwestern University.

Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Geshe Wangyal and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as professor at Amherst College (1973–1988) and director at Columbia University (1988–2019).

Robert A. Orsi is a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Trinity College and Yale University. He held academic posts at Fordham, Indiana University Bloomington, Harvard, Northwestern University, and the University of Notre Dame.
Robert Alan Goodding is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert Alexander Neil was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Aberdeen under William Duguid Geddes and at Peterhouse, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, later serving as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge from 1884.

Robert B. Ekvall was a Tibetology and history scholar. He served as a research fellow at the University of Washington (1958), a research associate at the University of Chicago (1958–1960), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (1963–1983).

Robert Baker Aitken was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Ryutaku-ji, and UC Berkeley under D.T. Suzuki and Hakuun Yasutani, and held posts at Besant Hill School and the East-West Center.

Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Tibet University, Columbia University (1999–2018), SOAS University of London, and King's College London.
